# SOP-P3-L4-01 Line startup - Heat Treat line

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, EQ-P3-L4-SB03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-026, MM-P3-L4-HT02, MM-P3-L4-SB03

Purpose
1. Define the required steps to perform a controlled startup of the Heat Treat line at P3-L4 following planned maintenance or an extended shutdown. This procedure addresses mechanical checks, safety verifications, sequence rationale, example observations and mandatory records.

Scope
2. Applies to operators, maintenance technicians and supervisors responsible for EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02 and EQ-P3-L4-SB03. Do not start the line without completing all preconditions and sign-offs described below.

Background and rationale
3. Heat Treat line startup requires coordinated confirmation of mechanical integrity, electrical readiness and safety systems to prevent damage to tooling and workpieces and to protect personnel. Specific fastener torques are critical for tool retention and safe operation; incorrect torque is a leading cause of component failure. The steps below sequence verification from isolation to live operation to minimize risk.

Preconditions (must be verified before Step 1)
4. a) Lockout/tagout (LOTO) for all power and energy sources completed and verified.  
b) All maintenance activities documented in ECN-2026-026 are closed or deferred with documented mitigation.  
c) Maintenance inspections and corrective actions recorded per MM-P3-L4-HT02 and MM-P3-L4-SB03 completed and signed off by responsible technician.  
d) Required spares and consumables available at the work area.  
e) Housekeeping and clear access to emergency stops confirmed.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
5. Minimum PPE for startup team: safety glasses with side shields, hearing protection, cut-resistant gloves for handling tooling, high-visibility vest, steel-toe footwear. Additional PPE required by MM-P3-L4-HT02 for heat treat operations must be worn when entering the HT furnace area.

Preparation and communications
6. Notify production control and area supervisor that startup is planned. Establish two-way communication between lead operator and maintenance technician. Post a visible startup tagboard at the line entry indicating status and point of contact.

Startup procedure — numbered steps
7. Step 1 — Visual mechanical inspection
- Verify guards and interlocks are secure and unobstructed.
- Inspect the mandrel and clamp area on EQ-P3-L4-RR01 for foreign objects or tooling misalignment. Clean as required.
- Inspect EQ-P3-L4-SB03 shot blast cabinet interior for loose liner material and debris.

8. Step 2 — Fastener torque verification (critical)
- Verify the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 605 N·m. If the torque is out of tolerance, do not proceed until corrected and rechecked. Record the measured value and the technician initials in the startup log.
- Verify the blast wheel liner bolt torque for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 90 N·m. If the torque is out of tolerance, do not proceed until corrected and rechecked. Record the measured value and the technician initials in the startup log.
Rationale: These torques secure rotating components and liners; incorrect torque can lead to catastrophic failure and secondary damage.

9. Step 3 — Functional interlock and sensor test (dry)
- With all power still isolated, operate manual function checks for safety interlocks, door switches, e-stops and emergency stops. Confirm wired and wireless alarms function. Document any failed items and correct per MM-P3-L4-HT02 before continuing.

10. Step 4 — Grease, lubrication and tooling
- Verify lubrication points on EQ-P3-L4-RR01 have been serviced per the MM reference and that lubricant type matches specification. Inspect tooling for wear; replace or rotate tooling if wear exceeds acceptable visual criteria per MM-P3-L4-HT02. Record part IDs and lot IDs in the maintenance log.

11. Step 5 — Low-power electrical energization (control power)
- Restore control power only. Verify control panels boot correctly and PLC interlocks report nominal. Confirm operator HMI displays correct status and no alarm conditions persist from pre-start checks. If fault persists, escalate to electrical maintenance.

12. Step 6 — No-load mechanical run
- With no workpieces loaded, command a slow jog of rotating assemblies and observe for abnormal vibration, noise or heat sources. Confirm that EQ-P3-L4-SB03 blast wheel runs smoothly and that EQ-P3-L4-RR01 mandrel rotation is concentric and free of runout that interferes with clamps or tooling. Stop immediately on abnormal signs and document findings.

13. Step 7 — Simulated process cycle
- Run a complete simulated cycle using a representative scrap or instrumented test piece. Verify sequence logic, tooling actuation, furnace pre-heat and conveyor operations operate in expected order. Monitor alarms and interlocks. If sequence deviations occur, review PLC logic and ECN-2026-026 for recent changes that may affect startup.

14. Step 8 — Initial loaded production
- Move to single-piece loaded production after satisfactory simulated cycle. The operator must remain at the local control during initial pieces and verify quality and mechanical stability. Monitor output and listen for new noises. If defects or unusual conditions arise, stop and investigate.

15. Step 9 — Ramp to normal production
- Ramp production volume only after sign-off by the line supervisor confirming the initial loaded production criteria are met and recorded.

Examples of observations and responses
16. Example: If a mandrel clamp bolt returns a torque reading below the required value, tighten to specification, re-torque and inspect clamp seating for wear. If seating damage is found, replace the clamp and document using MM-P3-L4-HT02 directives.  
Example: If the shot blast cabinet liner shows unusual wear pattern, capture photos, record liner bolt torque as per Step 2, and reference MM-P3-L4-SB03 for liner change procedure.

Records to keep
17. Maintain the following records in the line startup packet:
- Startup checklist with initials of responsible personnel.
- Torque verification log entries for the mandrel clamp bolt and blast wheel liner bolt including measured values and technician initials.
- Copies of any corrective maintenance orders generated and referenced to ECN-2026-026 when applicable.
- HMI alarm printouts or exported diagnostic logs during startup.
- Quality inspection results for initial production pieces.

Stop and notify
18. If any condition cannot be corrected by the on-site team, stop the startup and notify the area supervisor and maintenance planner. Log the reason for stop and reference ECN-2026-026 for any related engineering changes.

Responsibilities
19. Operators — perform steps, execute checks, and record results.  
Maintenance technicians — perform torque confirmation, corrective repairs and re-inspections.  
Supervisor — review results and provide final sign-off to enter normal production.

Sign-off (required)
20. Pre-start verification completed by:
- Lead Operator: Name: __________________ Signature: __________________ Date: __________
- Maintenance Technician: Name: __________________ Signature: __________________ Date: __________
- Line Supervisor: Name: __________________ Signature: __________________ Date: __________

Revision notes
21. See ECN-2026-026 for related engineering changes and MM-P3-L4-HT02 and MM-P3-L4-SB03 for detailed maintenance procedures and tooling specifications.
